# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent uses 13 LUTs and 6 FFs; simulation passes and hold slack is +0.091 ns, but setup WNS is −0.931 ns. The worst path runs from `rd_ptr` through distributed RAM read logic to `out_data[7]`, with clock insertion and pad delay also contributing. Timing recovery is the first objective; the current top requires `// @latency 1`, and no prior trial outcomes were supplied.

## Hypothesis

Registering the FIFO head and driving `out_data` directly from that register should remove the read-address-to-output path and may recover setup timing, at the cost of roughly WIDTH additional FFs and next-head selection logic.

## Instruction for generator

In `sync_fifo_core`, add a head-data register and replace the asynchronous `mem[rd_ptr]` output with a direct connection from that register; update it from `in_data` when a push makes the queue’s head, and from the next queued slot when a pop advances a nonempty queue. Handle simultaneous pop/push, including depth one and a full FIFO, so the new head is correct immediately after the edge; preserve the existing occupancy, ready/valid, reset, wrap, stall, and minimum-transfer-age behavior for every supported WIDTH and DEPTH. Keep `sync_fifo`’s interface and matching `// @latency 1` annotation, and keep `sync_fifo_core` defined and live-reached from the top.
